1#main: With what and how it is written. In it are 15 seifim. How they write the mezuzah: they write the two parashiyot of Shema and "Ve'hayah im shamo'a" on one page on one sheet; and make a space below and a space above like half a fingernail; and at its beginning leave enough to roll it after it is rolled. (And at its end one need not leave any at all) (Tur).
2#main: It must be written on one page; and if he wrote it on two or three pages, it is valid.
3#main: If he wrote it not in order—even if he forgot to write one letter—it is invalid and has no remedy; and needless to say if he put one parashah before the other.
4#main: If he wrote it on two hides—even though he sewed them—it is invalid.
5#main: It requires processing for its sake l'chatchila; but in a place where if he waits for hide processed for its sake the mitzvah will be nullified, he may write it on hide that is not processed that is found and fulfill the mitzvah immediately while seeking hide processed for its sake.
6#main: If he wrote it on klaf or on gevil, it is valid. They said "duchsustos" only for the optimal mitzvah. (And our klaf is valid for everything) (Mordechai, Hilchos Ketanim).
7#main: Its law regarding ink and writing and the adornment of shin-ayin-tet-nun-zayin-gimmel-tzadi is like a Sefer Torah.
8#main: It requires sirtut; and if he wrote it without sirtut, it is invalid.
9#main: He writes all its lines equal so one not be longer than its fellow; and if he lengthened one line more than the one before it and shortened the one beneath it more than the one before it, but before and after it is valid—provided he not make it like a dome or a tail or a circle.
10#main: Regarding "upon the earth"—he writes it at the head of the last line and writes no more on it.
11#main: They are accustomed to make it twenty-two lines.
12#main: It must be written with the right hand, as in tefillin.
13#main: The space between the parashah of Shema and the parashah of "Ve'hayah im shamo'a"—it is a mitzvah to make the latter a closed parashah; and if he made it open, it is valid, because it is not adjacent to it in the Torah.
14#main: One rolls it from its end to its beginning, from one side toward Shema.
15#main: It is forbidden to add anything to it except that on the outside they write "Shaddai" opposite the word "Ve'hayah" inside. {Rama: And some say opposite the space between the parashiyot (Tur in the name of the Rosh, Mordechai beginning of Hilchos Ketanim, Rambam, and Hagahos Maimoniyos in the name of Sefer HaTerumah); and so they practice, and place a hole in the reed opposite the name Shaddai so it be visible from outside (there in Mordechai and Hagahos Maimoniyos). They also practice writing on the outside kuzu bemuchsaz kuzu opposite "Hashem Elokeinu Hashem" (Tur), and one reverses these letters from the writing of the mezuzah so each letter align with the letter that substitutes for it in alfa-beisa (Hagahos Maimoniyos). But inside one may not add anything to the two parashiyot (Tur and Rambam).}
